az_gumby_wall.blurb: Gumby Wall is a small crag in the Mid-Mountain zone of Mt. Lemmon, up the Catalina Highway from Tucson, at roughly 7,700 feet among pines. Fourteen routes mix eleven bolted sport lines with three trad climbs, including a three-pitch outing. The spread is gentle: almost everything sits between 5.6 and 5.8, with one easier route and a lone 5.8 at the top of the range. That makes it a sensible place for a first lead or a relaxed day on moderate terrain. The rock is good quality and the bolting is generous, and the base is only a short stroll from the road.

az_pencil_thin_boulder.blurb: Pencil Thin Boulder is one block in the main cluster of the Beardsley boulder pile, a desert bouldering zone in the Phoenix area, sitting right beside Monkey Lust Boulder. It holds fourteen problems on coarse, weathered granite that is rough on fingertips. Grades run from an easy down-climb to V7, with the bulk between V3 and V5 and a handful of harder lines; expect thin flakes, arêtes and crimps. Some problems top out around 15 feet, so bring a pad and a spotter.

az_lost_world.blurb: Lost World is a small bouldering spot on the Copper Basin and Thumb Butte loop outside Prescott, at about 6,300 feet. Two main piles of boulders stand close to the dirt road, with more scattered down the drainage to the south. Views take in Thumb Butte and Granite Mountain, and water has sculpted some of the rocks into odd shapes. Of the fourteen problems, most are VB to V1, which suits beginners and warm-ups; a few sit around V2 and V3, and one standout reaches V6. The walk from the pullout is short, so it works well as a quick session.

az_tombstone.blurb: Tombstone is a small formation within Stewart Pocket, a granite-flavoured climbing zone east of Payson, at about 4,750 feet. Fourteen climbs are mostly trad, with a few bolted sport lines and a single aid route up the spire itself; the majority of the lines are on a big boulder just west of the spire. Grades mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with one very easy route and one 5.12 as the top end. Faces point in several directions, so some shade or sun is usually available. The approach crosses a large wash and follows a modest trail.

az_sun_wall.blurb: Sun Wall is a sport crag in the Virgin River Gorge, on the warm side of the canyon beside the Sun Cave, reached by crossing the river. All fourteen routes are bolted. The wall begins slightly less than vertical and steepens into overhanging ground past mid-height; the lower part is blocky, while the steeper upper sections have solid rock and tufas. The grades are hard: most climbs land in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, a couple go harder, and only a few easier lines exist at 5.7 to 5.11. Its sun makes it a good pick for cold winter days.

az_south_wall_4.blurb: South Wall is a granite cliff at Water Wheel Falls near Payson, rising on the far side of the East Verde River from the main trail. Fourteen routes, nine sport and five trad, run from 5.7 to the low 5.11s; the 5.11 range is the largest group, with seven climbs, backed by a few easier moderates and some 5.10s. Walls are tall, and a wide roof marks the start of the cliff. Reaching the first routes means a quick river hop and a scramble. This swimming-hole canyon draws many non-climbers, so the parking lot fills quickly on weekends.

az_funny_farm_the.blurb: The Funny Farm is a newer crag in Queen Creek Canyon near Superior, on the hillside south of the Atlantis wash. Fourteen routes combine eight sport lines with six trad, including a few multi-pitch options. Most climbs are moderate: nine fall at 5.7 or 5.8, a handful reach 5.10, and two sit in the 5.11 range. The rock favours small edges over pockets. The cliff is still being developed and loose rock is common, so wear a helmet, particularly at the base. A short trail leads down to the creek and then up to the wall.
